stories.title: 25-Year-Old CEO Marks 4 Years Since She Became the First Black Woman With Autism to Open a Locs & Wicks Bar
stories.summary: Aaliyah Alicia Thompson, diagnosed with autism at 5, became the first Black woman with autism to open a Locs & Wicks bar at 21. Now 25, she owns commercial property and runs a beauty school teaching kids and adults with autism entrepreneurial skills, proving autism is her strategy, not her limitation.
stories.extended_summary: At 22, Aaliyah Alicia Thompson walked into a closing and walked out with a deed, shocking a room full of adults as the first young Black woman with autism to buy commercial property in Jonesboro, Georgia. Her beauty school, housed in her own building, offers weekend trade classes for kids and adults with autism, building an entrepreneurship pipeline where less than 15% of autistic individuals are taught business skills. 'Autism is not my limitation; it is my strategy,' she says.

stories.extended_summary: As space missions stretch longer, scientists are asking how life beyond Earth affects the human body—and most research has focused on men. Dr. Begum Mathyk's team at USF Health changed that with a first-of-its-kind study on how parabolic flight affects the vaginal microbiome. The results, published in Frontiers in Microbiology, show that altered gravity and spaceflight stress can significantly disrupt vaginal microbial balance, while the oral microbiome remains largely stable. This early evidence suggests female biological systems respond uniquely to space conditions, underscoring the need for sex-specific research as we prepare for deep-space travel.
